newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: African leaders visit Kabila's Congo for summit.
newsitem.headline: African leaders visit Kabila's Congo for summit.

text.p: African heads of states gathered in Laurent Kabila's Congo on Sunday for an economic summit doubling as a show of solidarity for the new ruler of the former Zaire.

"It (my visit) should give solidarity to the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, to President Kabila," Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe, current chairman of the Organisation of African Unity, said on arrival.
"We support him in the process of transforming this country into democracy for economic prosperity," he told reporters at the Ndjili international airport in Kinshasa.

President Ange-Felix Patasse of neighbouring Central African Republic said the summit was part of Africa taking responsibility for its own affairs. "Africa has to take charge of itself. Such meetings have to be held now and then," he said.
Presidents Yoweri Museveni of Uganda and Pasteur Bizimungu of Rwanda, whose countries backed Kabila seven-month revolt that toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May, were present.
Others attending included Frederic Chiluba of Zambia, Joachim Chissano of Mozambique, Sam Nujoma of Namibia and Eritrea's Isayas Afewerki.
Ethiopia and Gabon were represented. Representatives of Tanzania, Burundi, Angola and Ghana were expected to attend.
Zaire, Africa's third largest nation is potentially one of its richest with a wealth of minerals and farmland. Over three decades of corruption under Mobutu left it impoverished.
